c: Part UUU of Chapter 58 of the Laws of 2020 § 5(c)

s: Calculate net paratransit operating expenses on a monthly basis.
q: Net paratransit operating expenses shall be calculated monthly by the MTA and will consist of the total paratransit operating expenses of the program minus the six percent of the urban tax dedicated to paratransit services as of the effective date of this subdivision and minus any money collected as passenger fares from paratransit operations.
c: Part UUU of Chapter 58 of the Laws of 2020 § 5(c)

s: Determine the schedule for payment of the city and state's capital funding shares to the MTA.

q: The city shall certify to the state comptroller and the New York state director of the budget, no later than seven days after making each payment pursuant to this section, the amount of the payments and the date upon which such payments were made.

s: Deposit all fees, fines and penalties collected under the AI companion article into the suicide prevention fund.
q: All fees, fines and penalties collected under this article shall be deposited into the suicide prevention fund as established pursuant to section ninety-nine-ss of the state finance law.

q: Moneys of the fund shall be made available to the office of mental health for initiatives supporting suicide prevention, education, and awareness.

q: There is hereby established in the joint custody of the comptroller, the commissioner of taxation and finance, and the office of mental health, a fund, to be known as the "suicide prevention fund".

q: The superintendent shall establish a process by which an entity described in this subdivision may request such authorization to act as a buy-now-pay-later lender, which process shall include, but not be limited to, requirements that the entity requesting such authorization submit a written plan describing the proposed buy-now-pay-later lending, its proposed policies and procedures for complying with the provisions of this article, and the impact on the overall business of the entity

s: Establish a process for withdrawing an authorization to act as a buy-now-pay-later lender.
q: The superintendent shall establish a process for withdrawing an authorization to act as a buy-now-pay-later lender.

q: if the superintendent finds that the financial responsibility, including meeting any capital requirements as established pursuant to subdivision three of this section, experience, character and general fitness of the applicant or any person associated with the applicant are such as to command the confidence of the community and to warrant the belief that the business will be conducted honestly, fairly and efficiently within the purposes and intent of this article, the superintendent shall issue the license

s: Direct the state comptroller to transfer, collect, or deposit funds equal to any unpaid city capital payment, pursuant to a filed plan.
q: the New York state director of the budget shall direct the state comptroller to transfer, collect, or deposit funds in accordance with subdivision (b) of this section in an amount equal to the unpaid balance of any payment required by section two of this act
ar: the New York state director of the budget

s: Notify an applicant of denial of a buy-now-pay-later lender license and retain the application fee.
q: If the superintendent refuses to issue a license, the superintendent shall notify the applicant of the denial and retain the fee paid pursuant to paragraph b of subdivision one of section seven hundred thirty-seven of this article.

s: Promulgate rules and regulations setting capital requirements to ensure the solvency and financial integrity of buy-now-pay-later licensees.
q: The superintendent shall promulgate rules and regulations setting capital requirements to ensure the solvency and financial integrity of licensees and their ongoing operations, taking into account the risks, volume of business, complexity, and other relevant factors regarding such licensees.

s: Issue licenses that state the licensee's name and address, and for partnerships, associations or corporations, the relevant identifying details.
q: A license issued under this article shall state the name and address of the licensee, and if the licensee be a co-partnership or association, the names of the members thereof, and for a corporation, the date and place of its incorporation.

s: Approve or disapprove a proposed change of control of a licensee.
q: The superintendent shall approve or disapprove the proposed change of control of a licensee in accordance with the provisions of section seven hundred thirty-eight of this article.

s: Execute a written order whenever revoking or suspending a license.
q: Whenever the superintendent shall revoke or suspend a license issued under this article, the superintendent shall forthwith execute a written order to that effect, which order may be reviewed in the manner provided by article seventy-eight of the civil practice law and rules.

s: Establish a maximum cumulative amount of all charges and fees a buy-now-pay-later lender can charge a consumer per loan category.
q: The superintendent shall establish a maximum cumulative amount of all charges and fees that a buy-now-pay-later lender can charge a consumer in connection with each category of buy-now-pay-later loans.

s: Make the transfers, collections and deposits as soon as practicable, no more than 3 days after the director of the budget's plan is transmitted.
q: The state comptroller is hereby authorized and directed to make such transfers, collections and deposits as soon as practicable but not more than 3 days following the transmittal of such plan to the comptroller in accordance with subdivision (a) of this section

s: Promulgate rules and regulations regarding the manner of charging interest and fees.
q: The superintendent shall promulgate rules and regulations regarding the manner of charging interest and fees as prescribed as in this section.

s: Must consider the applicability of other articles of the banking law when promulgating rules to avoid conflicting requirements.
q: When promulgating rules and regulations under this article, the superintendent shall consider the applicability of other articles of this chapter to buy-now-pay-later lenders and buy-now-pay-later loans for the purpose of avoiding conflicting requirements.

s: Must not impose or collect a penalty under this article if a penalty was already imposed under another chapter provision for the same act.
q: The superintendent shall not impose or collect any penalty for an act or omission constituting a violation of this article if the superintendent imposes or collects any penalty pursuant to another provision of this chapter for the same act or omission.

s: Must not impose a penalty more than once for the same act or omission by different entities unless both knowingly committed it.
q: The superintendent shall not impose or collect a penalty for an act or omission constituting a violation of this article by a buy-now-pay-later lender more than once for the same act or omission, where the entity extending credit directly to a consumer is different from the entity operating a platform, software, or system with which the consumer interacts, unless both entities are found to have knowingly committed the same act or omission.

s: Keep confidential reports of examinations and investigations concerning licensed buy-now-pay-later lenders, among other covered entities, unless disclosure serves the ends of justice.
q: licensed lender, licensed buy-now-pay-later lender, licensed casher of checks, licensed mortgage banker, registered mortgage broker, licensed mortgage loan originator, licensed sales finance company, registered mortgage loan servicer, licensed student loan servicer, licensed insurance premium finance agency, licensed transmitter of money, licensed budget planner, any other person or entity subject to supervision under this chapter, or the department, shall be confidential communications, shall not be subject to subpoena and shall not be made public unless, in the judgment of the superintendent, the ends of justice and the public advantage will be subserved by the publication thereof

s: Monitor the degree and continued existence of competition and the effectiveness of flexible rating for for-hire motor vehicle insurance on an ongoing basis.
q: The superintendent shall monitor the degree and continued existence of competition and the effectiveness of flexible rating in this state on an on-going basis.

q: The dormitory authority of the state of New York shall provide a report providing information regarding any project undertaken pursuant to a design and construction management agreement, as authorized by part BB of chapter 58 of the laws of 2012, between the dormitory authority of the state of New York and the department of environmental conservation and/or the office of parks, recreation and historic preservation to the governor, the temporary president of the senate and speaker of the assembly.
c: Section 2 of Part GG of the act

ar: The director of the division of minority and women's business development

s: Expand the annual procurement report to distinguish by contract type awards made under the expanded non-competitive purchase authority and specify totals, values and percentages compared to the prior reporting period.

s: Submit written notice to the governor and legislative leaders when filing an application to form a pure captive insurance company.

q: Prior to forming such captive insurance company, the corporation or its subsidiary shall complete a feasibility study including, but not limited to, an analysis of the actuarial risks and feasibility associated with the creation of the insurance captive, a measurement of value of such insurance captives relative to financing risk utilizing commercial insurance or self-financing, including in the aggregate and by respective insurance type, the advantages and disadvantages of potential insurance captive structures, and a domicile analysis.

a: New York Convention Center Operating Corporation
s: Provide the completed feasibility study to the temporary president of the senate, the speaker of the assembly, and the governor.
q: Such feasibility study shall be provided to the temporary president of the senate, the speaker of the assembly, and the governor upon completion, and shall be conducted by an independent risk consultant firm or captive insurance broker licensed by the state to perform such duties.

s: Review registry information concerning the county, after consulting all cities, towns and villages within its jurisdiction, and provide the department with corrections or supplements regarding suspected inactive hazardous waste disposal sites.
q: Each county, after consultation with all cities, towns, and villages within its jurisdiction, shall review the information concerning such county in the registry established pursuant to section 27-1305 of this article

s: Cooperate and coordinate with local jurisdictions, regional organizations or state agencies to fulfill their responsibilities to identify and report inactive hazardous waste disposal sites.
q: Counties shall cooperate and coordinate with local jurisdictions, regional organizations or state agencies to fulfill its responsibilities under subdivisions one and two of this section

q: Such memorandum shall address, for purposes of such demonstration program, the use of systems, devices and other facilities owned and operated by the state, covered agencies, and covered authorities.
ar: The New York state department of transportation, covered agencies, and covered authorities

s: Survey the county's jurisdiction to locate suspected inactive hazardous waste disposal sites, consult with cities, towns and villages, and annually report findings to the department.
q: Commencing one year after the effective date of this paragraph, each county shall, for the purpose of locating inactive hazardous waste disposal sites, survey its jurisdiction to determine the existence and location of suspected inactive hazardous waste disposal sites and shall, after consultation with all cities, towns, and villages within its jurisdiction, annually thereafter submit a report to the department describing the location of each such suspected site and the reasons for such suspicion.

s: Maintain a statewide registry of inactive hazardous waste disposal sites on its website, in addition to regional and county-level public inspection copies.
q: a registry of inactive hazardous waste disposal sites in such region or, with respect to the office of the county clerk or register, in such county, or with respect to its website, the entire state.

s: Include in the registry whether a site is located within a disadvantaged community as part of address and site boundary information.
q: Address and site boundaries including tax map parcel numbers or section, block and lot numbers, and if the site is located within a disadvantaged community.

s: Annually assess and reassess, by March 31, the need for remedial action at each site, including whether sites should be prioritized due to location in a disadvantaged community.
q: The department shall, as part of the registry, assess and, based upon new information received, reassess by March thirty-first of each year, in cooperation with the department of health, the relative need for action at each site to remedy environmental and health problems resulting from the presence of hazardous wastes at such sites including in such assessment whether sites shall be prioritized under subdivision five of this section due to site location in an area identified as a disadvantaged community

s: Prioritize remedial programs at classification 1 or 2 sites located in disadvantaged communities.
q: The department shall, in accordance with subdivision five of this section, prioritize remedial programs at sites placed in classification 1 or 2, as described in clauses (i) and (ii) of subparagraph one of this paragraph, that are located in disadvantaged communities, consistent with the protection of public health and the environment.

s: Publish hearing notices for registry disputes in the environmental notice bulletin, on the department's website, and in a local newspaper.
q: No less than thirty days prior to the hearing the commissioner shall cause a notice of hearing to be published in the next available environmental notice bulletin, on the department's website, and in a newspaper of general circulation in the county in which the site is located.

s: Notify in writing the site owner or operator and owners of record of adjacent properties before a hearing.
q: The commissioner shall also notify in writing any owner or operator of the site, as well as the owners of record of adjacent properties, no less than thirty days prior to the hearing.

s: Publish notice of a proposed site deletion from the registry on the department's website, in the environmental notice bulletin, and in a local newspaper.
q: Such notice of deletion shall be published in the next available environmental notice bulletin, on the department's website, and in a newspaper of general circulation in the county in which the site is located.

s: Summarize public comments on proposed deletions and make the summary available on the department's website.
q: The commissioner shall summarize any comments received and make the summary available to the public on the department's website.

s: Notify all public repositories of the registry, including updating its website, of any modifications or deletions.
q: The department shall notify, as soon as possible and within available resources all public repositories of the registry, including updating its website, of any modifications or deletions to such registry.

s: Submit and publish site cleanup prioritization criteria to the governor, legislature, and the department's website by January 1, 2026.
q: The department shall, no later than January first, two thousand twenty-six, submit to the governor and legislature and publish on its website site cleanup prioritization criteria.

s: Review and update site cleanup prioritization criteria as necessary.
q: The department shall review and update criteria as necessary.

s: Submit and publish an annual inactive hazardous waste remedial program status report, including a financial accounting, to the governor, legislature, and the department's website by December 31 each year.
q: The department no later than December thirty-first of each year, shall, using the information available to it, submit to the governor and legislature, and make public on the department's website an inactive hazardous waste remedial program status report for the previous fiscal year.

s: Develop a system to prioritize sites for remedial action that incorporates environmental, natural resource, public health, and disadvantaged-community location factors.
q: Such system shall incorporate environmental, natural resource and public health concerns, and a site's location within a disadvantaged community.

s: Prioritize implementation of inactive hazardous waste remedial programs in accordance with the site prioritization system.
q: The department shall prioritize implementation of remedial programs in accordance with subdivision five of section 27-1305 of this title.

s: Consider, among other factors, whether remedial actions would benefit a disadvantaged community when determining the scope of a remedial program.
q: the extent to which the actions would reduce such danger to human health or the environment or would otherwise benefit human health or the environment, including if the actions would benefit a disadvantaged community

s: Make every effort to secure response costs, natural resource damages, and penalties from persons responsible for disposal of hazardous waste at a site where the department implemented a remedial program.

s: Make every effort to secure response costs, natural resource damages, and penalties from the owner, operator, or other responsible person for a site.

s: Notify the department of any release of hazardous waste within ten days of obtaining actual knowledge of such release, when the municipality has taken possession of, owns, or operates a site under this exemption.

ar: any municipality or public corporation that has taken possession of a site

s: Prioritize recovery of response costs and natural resource damages at classification 1 or 2 sites in disadvantaged communities.
q: The commissioner shall prioritize recovering response costs and natural resource damages at sites placed in classification 1 or 2, as described in clauses (i) and (ii) of subparagraph one of paragraph b of subdivision two of section 27-1305 of this title, that are located in disadvantaged communities.

s: Prohibits state employees from disclosing an individual's personally identifiable information to immigration authorities.
q: No state employee shall disclose to an immigration authority or any employee thereof an individual's personally identifiable information, including, but not limited to, a person's name, social security number, physical description, any associated addresses, telephone number, financial information, medical information, or place of employment or education except as provided in subdivision nine of this section.
